questions.q: Why does scrolling social media keep us hooked?
a: Each swipe brings less pleasure, so we seek more
The app rewards us with money and prizes
Our brains stop producing dopamine entirely
Notifications arrive at unpredictable times only
questions.why: Lesson 1 says dopamine gives intense pleasure, but the payoff shrinks with repetition, driving the habit.

questions.q: How does using your phone in bed affect sleep?
a: The light tells your body it is time to be awake
It makes you fall asleep faster by relaxing you
It has no effect as long as you use dark mode
It improves sleep by blocking outside noise
questions.why: Lesson 1 says phone light signals wakefulness and teaches your mind the bed is for being conscious.

questions.q: How long does it take to regain deep focus after a distraction?
a: About 25 minutes
About 5 minutes
About 15 minutes
About 40 minutes
questions.why: Lesson 2 cites an estimate of 25 minutes to get back into deep work after an interruption.

questions.q: What does the summary recommend doing with email notifications?
a: Turn them off and check email at set times
Answer each one immediately to stay ahead
Keep only the alerts from your manager
Check email first thing every morning
questions.why: Lesson 2 suggests silencing notifications and setting aside specific times to respond.

questions.q: How does the summary suggest breaking a phone habit?
a: Replace the routine part of the habit loop
Quit all devices for a full month
Delete every social media account
Set a strict daily screen time limit
questions.why: Lesson 3 says swapping the routine, like picking up a book instead, works better than quitting cold turkey.
